psy-major-depressive-disorder.title: Major depressive disorder
psy-major-depressive-disorder.blurb: Six weeks of low mood, confirmed with structured screening with direct safety assessment.
psy-major-depressive-disorder.summary: Major depressive disorder presents with six weeks of low mood, poor sleep, and loss of interest in hobbies, typically with flat affect with psychomotor slowing and passive death wish, without plan. Structured screening with direct safety assessment confirms it, and an antidepressant with psychotherapy and scheduled follow-up is the initial management.

sections.heading: Overview
paras: The presentation that names major depressive disorder is six weeks of low mood, poor sleep, and loss of interest in hobbies; the process behind it is dysregulated monoamine signaling within mood circuits. Sections below follow one conventional sequence — mechanism, presentation, confirmation, management — and each can be read on its own.

How often the problem is seen depends on where the counting is done, and case definitions have shifted enough over time that historical series need reading with care. The teaching point most often attached to this topic is that asking directly about suicide does not plant the idea — it opens the only door to safety.

sections.heading: Mechanism
paras: The process at work is dysregulated monoamine signaling within mood circuits. Its consequences account for both the symptoms the patient reports and the signs found on examination.

Reserve within the affected system means measurable derangement often precedes anything the patient notices. Understanding this is what makes an antidepressant with psychotherapy and scheduled follow-up the rational first response rather than an arbitrary one.

sections.heading: Clinical presentation
paras: The history classically centres on six weeks of low mood, poor sleep, and loss of interest in hobbies; what refines it is the time course rather than the severity at any one moment.

Presentations at the extremes of age are frequently less typical, and a normal early course does not exclude the diagnosis. A history of six weeks of low mood, poor sleep, and loss of interest in hobbies in the right context is enough to bring the diagnosis to the front of the differential.

sections.heading: Examination
paras: Flat affect with psychomotor slowing and passive death wish, without plan is the examination finding that most reliably separates this from its closest mimics.
Interobserver agreement for the classic signs is only moderate, which is a reason to weigh them alongside the history rather than above it.

sections.heading: Diagnosis
paras: The first investigation is structured screening with direct safety assessment; ordering it early avoids a sequence of tests that each exclude one possibility.

Testing before the pre-test probability has been thought through produces results that are difficult to act on in either direction. The alternative most often confused with it is obsessive-compulsive disorder, which is compared below.

Reported frequency varies with the population studied and with the threshold chosen to define a case, so figures quoted in different sources are rarely directly comparable.
